title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 15-17). Grothendieck is building an axiomatic 'analysis situs' for tame ('modérée') topology. It is based on a set F_el of elementary figures (strata), a refinement order ≪, a compatibility relation, and the derived order ≤ (x ≤ x' iff x ≪ x' and x, x' are compatible). On p.15 he defines a subdivision of a figure F as a refinement F' of F (every piece of F' lies in a piece of F) that is maximal among refinements of F. On p.15 the maximality is for ⊂; on p.16 it is for ≤. Page 16 justifies that this agrees with the intuitive notion: a subdivision is a refinement with the same support.

Claim. Let F be a stratification of X = |F| and F' a refinement of F with support X' = |F'| ≠ |F|, so X' is a proper closed tame subset of X. Then F' is not maximal among refinements of F.

Construction. Build F'' ⊋ F' refining F with |F''| = |F|. Its strata are:
(a) the strata U_j of F';
(b) the nonempty connected components V_{iα} of U_i \ (U_i ∩ X'), where U_i runs over the strata of F.
Then F'' refines F, since V_{iα} ⊂ U_i. It contains F' strictly, since some V_{iα} is nonempty because X' ≠ X. Its support is ∪U_i = |F|.

What must be checked. F'' must be a stratification, i.e. satisfy the frontier condition: ∂V_{iα} := closure(V_{iα}) \ V_{iα} must be a union of strata. Inside U_i this means: the frontier of each connected component of U_i \ X' in U_i, which lies in X' ∩ U_i, must be a union of strata of F'. He isolates this as 'a problem which looks interesting, of the topology of a stratified space (X'∩U_i) inside a (tame) manifold (U_i)'.

Margin. He wants to state first that a maximal refinement has |F'| = |F|. More generally: for any refinement F' of F there is a refinement F'' of F with |F''| = |F| and F''|_{X'} = F'. That is, a stratification of a closed tame subspace, compatible with F, extends to a subdivision of F.

Modern reading. This is the 'extension of a stratification of a closed subset to the ambient space' lemma. In Whitney/Thom–Mather or o-minimal settings it follows from local conical structure. Along a stratum S of X' ∩ U_i, the set of points of S adherent to a given complementary component is open (local triviality) and closed in S, hence all of S since S is connected.
errors: Gap: only ∂V_{iα} ∩ U_i is addressed. The part of ∂V_{iα} lying in ∂U_i, i.e. in lower strata U_j of F that are themselves cut into F'-strata and components V_{jβ}, must also be a union of F''-strata. This needs the same local-triviality argument applied across the strata of F and is not discussed.

The key step (frontier of a complementary component of a stratified subset of a manifold is a union of strata) is left open. It holds under local topological triviality (Whitney (b) / Thom–Mather, or o-minimal trivialization). Under a bare frontier-condition axiom it is not automatic, and the page does not say which axioms of the 'contrée' guarantee it.
Minor: on p.15 maximality is with respect to ⊂, on p.16 with respect to ≤; the two are conflated.

ideas.what: Subdivision of a stratification defined intrinsically as a maximal refinement, and proof that maximal refinements have full support
ideas.modern_name: subdivision / refinement of stratifications (poset of stratifications)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in PL topology and stratification theory (Whitney, Thom, Mather; o-minimal: van den Dries)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 only calls for a tame-topology foundation; this axiomatic definition is not published

ideas.what: Extending a stratification of a closed tame subset X' ⊂ |F| (compatible with F) to a stratification of all of |F| by adding the connected components of the complements in each stratum
ideas.modern_name: compatible stratification / cell decomposition adapted to finitely many definable subsets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Łojasiewicz, Whitney, Thom–Mather; o-minimal cell decomposition (Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn, van den Dries)

ideas.what: Problem: in a tame manifold U, the frontier of each component of U \ Y (Y a closed stratified subset) is a union of strata of Y
ideas.modern_name: consequence of local conic structure / topological local triviality of stratified sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom–Mather (Whitney stratified sets); o-minimal trivialization theorem (Hardt, van den Dries)

missed.claim: Grothendieck flags as 'interesting' the question of which minimal axioms on a stratified subspace of a tame manifold force complementary components to have frontiers that are unions of strata. Read in his axiomatic 'contrée' framework (without assuming Whitney regularity), this is a question about the minimal axiom set for tame topology. It was not pursued in this form, but its content is essentially covered by known local-triviality theorems.
missed.quote: il y a un pb, qui a l'air intéressant, de topologie d'un espace stratifié (X'∩U_i) dans une variété (top. modérée) (U_i)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginal. It is relevant only to attempts to axiomatize Grothendieck's tame topology combinatorially (e.g. via posets of strata / exit-path categories), where one wants frontier properties derived from combinatorial axioms rather than from Whitney conditions.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but foundational lemma in Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatics of tame stratified spaces. The mathematics (subdivisions have full support; stratifications of a closed subset extend to the ambient space) is standard in stratification and o-minimal theory. Its main interest is as documentation of the 1986 'Analysis situs' project.
transcription_corrections: 'Fonction [?] des V_{iα} dans U_i' should read 'Frontière des V_{iα} dans U_i' (⊂ X'∩U_i).
The displayed equation is most likely '|F'| ≠ |F| = |F''|', with X' under |F'| and X under |F|, not '|F'| ∪ |F| = |F'|'.
'(top. [?] modérée)' is 'top. modérée', i.e. tame topology.
'd'une [?] ∂V_{iα}' is likely 'd'où ∂V_{iα} ... est réunion de strates'.
Line 'Car on définira un raffinement de F', [?] conjugué' is likely 'on définira un raffinement F'' de F, qui est ... et qui contient F''; 'conjugué' is doubtful.
